entries.title: Luke 18:1
segments: Jesus told his disciples a parable to show them that they should always pray and never despair.

entries.title: Luke 18:2
segments: "There was," he said, "in a certain town a judge, who had no fear of God nor regard for man.

entries.title: Luke 18:3
segments: In the same town there was a widow who went to him again and again, and said 'Grant me justice against my opponent.'

entries.title: Luke 18:4
segments: For a time the judge refused, but afterwards he said to himself 'Although I am without fear of God or regard for man,

entries.title: Luke 18:5
segments: Yet, as this widow is so troublesome, I will grant her justice, to stop her from plaguing me with her endless visits.'"

entries.title: Luke 18:6
segments: Then the Master added: "Listen to what this iniquitous judge says!

entries.title: Luke 18:7
segments: And God--will not he see that his own People, who cry to him night and day, have justice done them--though he holds his hand?

entries.title: Luke 18:8
segments: He will, I tell you, have justice done them, and that soon! Yet, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth?"

entries.title: Luke 18:9
segments: Another time, speaking to people who were satisfied that they were religious, and who regarded every one else with scorn, Jesus told this parable--

entries.title: Luke 18:10
segments: "Two men went up into the Temple Courts to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other a tax-gatherer.

entries.title: Luke 18:11
segments: The Pharisee stood forward and began praying to himself in this way--'O God, I thank thee that I am not like other men-- thieves, rogues, adulterers--or even like this tax-gatherer.

entries.title: Luke 18:12
segments: I fast twice a week, and give a tenth of everything I get to God.'

entries.title: Luke 18:13
segments: Meanwhile the tax-gatherer stood at a distance, not venturing even 'to raise his eyes to Heaven'; but he kept striking his breast and saying 'O God, have mercy on me, a sinner.'

entries.title: Luke 18:14
segments: This man, I tell you, went home pardoned, rather than the other; for every one who exalts himself will be humbled, while every one who humbles himself shall be exalted."

entries.title: Luke 18:15
segments: Some of the people were bringing even their babies to Jesus, for him to touch them; but, when the disciples saw it, they began to find fault with those who had brought them.

entries.title: Luke 18:16
segments: Jesus, however, called the little children to him. "Let the little children come to me," he said, "and do not hinder them; for it is to the childlike that the Kingdom of God belongs.

entries.title: Luke 18:17
segments: I tell you, unless a man receives the Kingdom of God like a child, he will not enter it at all."

entries.title: Luke 18:18
segments: And one of the Presidents asked Jesus this question--"Good Teacher, what must I do if I am to gain Immortal Life?"

entries.title: Luke 18:19
segments: "Why do you call me good?" answered Jesus. "No one is good but God.

entries.title: Luke 18:20
segments: You know the commandments--'Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not say what is false about others, Honor thy father and thy mother.'"

entries.title: Luke 18:21
segments: "I have observed all these," he replied, "from childhood."

entries.title: Luke 18:22
segments: Hearing this, Jesus said to him: "There is one thing still lacking in you; sell everything that you have, and distribute to the poor, and you shall have wealth in Heaven; then come and follow me."

entries.title: Luke 18:23
segments: But the man became greatly distressed on hearing this, for he was extremely rich.

entries.title: Luke 18:24
segments: Seeing this, Jesus said to his disciples: "How hard it is for men of wealth to enter the Kingdom of God!

entries.title: Luke 18:25
segments: It is easier, indeed, for a camel to get through a needle's eye than for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of God!"

entries.title: Luke 18:26
segments: "Then who can be saved?" asked those who heard this.

entries.title: Luke 18:27
segments: But Jesus said: "What is impossible with men is possible with God."

entries.title: Luke 18:28
segments: "But we," said Peter, "we left what belonged to us and followed you."

entries.title: Luke 18:29
segments: "I tell you," he answered, "that there is no one who has left house, or wife, or brothers, or parents, or children, on account of the Kingdom of God,

entries.title: Luke 18:30
segments: Who will not receive many times as much in the present, and in the age that is coming Immortal Life."

entries.title: Luke 18:31
segments: Gathering the Twelve round him, Jesus said to them: "Listen! We are going up to Jerusalem; and there everything that is written in the Prophets will be done to the Son of Man.

entries.title: Luke 18:32
segments: For he will be given up to the Gentiles, mocked, insulted and spat upon;

entries.title: Luke 18:33
segments: They will scourge him, and then put him to death; and on the third day he will rise again."

entries.title: Luke 18:34
segments: The Apostles did not comprehend any of this; his meaning was unintelligible to them, and they did not understand what he was saying.

entries.title: Luke 18:35
segments: As Jesus was getting near Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the road-side, begging.

entries.title: Luke 18:36
segments: Hearing a crowd going by, the man asked what was the matter;

entries.title: Luke 18:37
segments: And, when people told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing,

entries.title: Luke 18:38
segments: He shouted out: "Jesus, Son of David, take pity on me!"

entries.title: Luke 18:39
segments: Those who were in front kept telling him to be quiet, but he continued to call out the louder: "Son of David, take pity on me!"

entries.title: Luke 18:40
segments: Then Jesus stopped and ordered the man to be brought to him. And, when he had come close up to him, Jesus asked him:

entries.title: Luke 18:41
segments: "What do you want me to do for you?" "Master," he said, "I want to recover my sight."

entries.title: Luke 18:42
segments: And Jesus said: "Recover your sight, your faith has delivered you."

entries.title: Luke 18:43
segments: Instantly he recovered his sight, and began to follow Jesus, praising God. And all the people, on seeing it, gave glory to God.
